item.title: Busta Rhymes Returns To His Old Brooklyn School For Thanksgiving Giveaway
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Busta Rhymes returned to his old East Flatbush school, where hundreds of families got holiday food, coats and other essentials.
item.content:encoded:
Busta Rhymes went back to his old elementary school on November 21 to help East Flatbush families get ready for Thanksgiving and winter. The rapper joined Assemblywoman Monique Chandler-Waterman and the IAmWondaWoman Foundation at P.S. 135 for the third annual Busta Rhymes Brooklyn Day, where hundreds of families received help ahead of the holiday.

Families picked up turkeys, winter coats, clothing and other essentials, PIX11 reported from the event. Workshops on housing, mental health and gun violence ran alongside the distribution. The foundation’s giveaway predates the event honoring the rapper: Saturday also marked its 18th annual community giveaway.

Busta told PIX11 he had been a student at P.S. 135 and saw the visit as a way to give back to a neighborhood that had given him much. He said it “molded and shaped me to become the man that I am, the father that I am, the friend that I am.”

The assemblywoman’s district calendar put the giveaway and Busta Rhymes Day together at the school on Linden Boulevard. The calendar listed the giveaway from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. at the corner of Linden and Schenectady avenues. Busta recalls the neighborhood and the people he looked up to growing up in the WayMaker interview below.

The school has been part of the event from the beginning. FOX 5 New York covered the first edition in 2024, when Busta performed as well as helping with the turkey giveaway. At that first celebration, Brooklyn Borough President Antonio Reynoso proclaimed November 23 a day honoring Busta Rhymes, Caribbean Life reported from the event. “We give back to the community regularly because it’s home, and it’s not really something that we do for recognition,” Busta told FOX 5 that year.

People at that first giveaway could also sit in on a mental health workshop and a session on the state’s Black studies curriculum.

He came back to P.S. 135 in 2025, when AllHipHop reported that he made an unannounced appearance and helped hand out food.

In 2025, the volunteers packed the giveaway with more than turkeys, distributing vegetables, potatoes and other pantry staples.

item.title: Dave East Joins North Philly In Remembering D. Jones
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Dave East joined hundreds in North Philadelphia to pay tribute to D. Jones, whose family released balloons in his honor.
item.content:encoded:
D. Jones brought hundreds of people together in North Philadelphia on November 21, a week after the rapper was killed.

His family and friends held a celebration of life, and his longtime friend and recording partner Dave East came to remember the man they knew as Jonesy.

Loved ones released balloons during the gathering, CBS Philadelphia reported. Jones’ mother, Yolanda Jones, told the station what it felt like to see so many people come out for her son: “It makes my heart so full.”

“Nobody could say nothing bad about him,” Dave East told the station.

Dave East and D. Jones had years of records together by the time they worked on “The Meaning” for Still Counting Blessings in 2025.

They recorded “Wooh” with Jadakiss in 2020, and Jones appeared on Dave East’s Karma 2 track “This Summer” two years earlier.

Jones was making music at home long before those records.

He came up in Philadelphia’s street DVD era with the Go Gettas and appeared in Young Bob’s Headshots series.

He later brought those local roots to records with New York rappers and took his music overseas, recalling a London trip with The LOX on his own channel.

Dave East was also on the same stage this summer at Jones’ sold-out Lifers Fest at The Foundry in Philadelphia, alongside Young Chris and Freeway.

Jones followed the hometown show with Definition of a Lifer, a seven-song project released in September.

Police said Jones was not involved in the road-rage dispute that led to the November 14 shooting, which killed him at 42.

Daniel Dickerson was arrested and faces a murder charge and other offenses in the case.

Jones’ loved ones told the Inquirer they plan to go ahead with a December 4 night of music at VOIX Karaoke, where he’d been due to perform.

item.title: BigXthaPlug Wins First BMI Country Award For Bailey Zimmerman Collab
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: BigXthaPlug and producer Bandplay earned their first BMI Country Awards for the Bailey Zimmerman crossover "All The Way."
item.content:encoded:
BigXthaPlug picked up his first BMI Country Award as a songwriter for “All The Way,” the track he made with Bailey Zimmerman.

BMI also recognized producer Krishon “Bandplay” Gaines and fellow writers Jenna Johnson and KK Johnson as first-time winners for the same song.

BMI announced the honors during a ceremony in Nashville.

The four were among 38 writers receiving their first BMI Country Awards. The organization recognizes the writers and publishers of the country songs that drew the most performances over the previous year.

Zimmerman’s part in the ceremony was a performance of “What Hurts The Most” for Jeffrey Steele, who co-wrote that song and received the BMI Icon Award.

BigXthaPlug had the track before Zimmerman joined.

“I actually made the song probably like two years ago. We knew that we wanted to do a project,” he told Billboard’s Jessica Nicholson in an interview with Zimmerman.

He said other artists had expressed interest, but Zimmerman was one of the people who put his voice on it and sent it back.

Zimmerman said he already knew from Instagram that the Dallas rapper wanted to make a country project.

He said he recorded his part in about 10 minutes once BigXthaPlug sent the track over. On the finished song, Zimmerman sings the hook while BigXthaPlug handles the verses, with steel guitar and trap drums in the same arrangement.

“All The Way” was released in April 2025 and entered Billboard’s Hot Country Songs chart at No. 1. It was the rapper’s first appearance on that chart and Zimmerman’s first No. 1 there.

Billboard reported 24.1 million official U.S. streams in its opening week, when it also reached No. 3 on Hot Rap Songs. BMI had already recognized the song at its R&B/Hip-Hop Awards in August.

The track led into I Hope You’re Happy, which paired BigXthaPlug with Jelly Roll and Ella Langley, among others.

BigXthaPlug’s next album went in a different direction: Better Over Time, his first No. 1 on Billboard’s Top Rap Albums chart.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Feds Ask Judge To Strike Big U’s Filing Challenging Wiretap
item.dc:creator: Grouchy Greg Watkins (@GrouchyGreg)
item.description: Prosecutors asked to strike and seal Big U's defense filing, which disputes how agents described an alleged $30,000 demand.
item.content:encoded:
Big U‘s lawyers challenged the account federal agents used to obtain a wiretap on his phone, and prosecutors want the defense filing struck and sealed.

The dispute in his Los Angeles racketeering case centers on a $30,000 demand that the government has described as extortion and the defense says was an argument about payment for an appearance.

Defense attorney Charles C. Brown laid out that account in a declaration obtained by AllHipHop.com.

According to the agent’s allegations, Big U demanded $30,000 for appearing at a birthday event and threatened that he and others “would tear up the club” if he didn’t get paid.

Brown disputed what the cited call showed.

“The December 2 call was provided to the Title III Court entirely out of context,” he wrote. Brown said Big U was frustrated that his name was being used to promote a party and that artists were being advertised without being available.

Brown also wrote that the defense interviewed a witness who said he had not been robbed or extorted.

According to Brown’s account of that interview, uncertainty over an appearance fee led to a discussion that ended with an agreement over how much Big U would receive.

Brown says the disputed conversation was used in the original criminal complaint.

He asked the judge to order prosecutors to produce records of any government contact with the witness, with private review by the judge if necessary.

The filing was part of the defense’s effort to keep intercepted conversations out of evidence in the Central District of California.

The Los Angeles music executive, whose legal name is Eugene Henley Jr., has pleaded not guilty in the federal case, which includes racketeering and extortion charges.

The new dispute follows an earlier fight over when the trial should start.

item.title: Chuck D Explains Why He Called Drake The Elton John Of Rap
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Chuck D explained why he compared Drake to Elton John, pointing to how far their records traveled rather than how they sounded.
item.content:encoded:
Chuck D called Drake the Elton John of rap, then explained what he meant: the two artists don’t sound alike, but both make music that reaches well outside their original audiences.

The Public Enemy frontman made the comparison on X on November 21 and followed up with a series of replies.

“I experienced the 1970s … @Drake is unquestionably the Elton John of Rap,” he wrote.

When asked to explain the comparison, Chuck narrowed it down to “Popular relevance and cultural saturation.”

In that reply, he pointed to Elton’s singing, piano playing and co-written radio records. With Drake, he pointed instead to the call-and-response that happens when arena crowds know the records well enough to join in.

Chuck also pushed back on the idea that calling someone the Elton John of rap was a dig.

He recalled hearing Elton on AM radio, from “Your Song” to “Philadelphia Freedom.”

“I like them both and see similarities,” he wrote in another reply.

The singles Chuck named came from different points in Elton’s rise.

“Your Song” was his first UK hit, according to the Official Charts Company. Elton’s own site notes that “Philadelphia Freedom” was released in 1975 without an album attached and went to No. 1 in the United States.

It later appeared on his second greatest hits collection.

Drake’s older records were still sitting alongside his new ones on the Billboard 200 dated November 21.

Take Care, released in 2011, came in at No. 14 in its 715th chart week. This year’s Iceman was one place ahead of it.

Chuck has seen how the way people hear music can change.

In an AllHipHop interview with broadcaster Lady B, he discussed the early fight to get Hip-Hop onto daytime radio.

Chuck has credited his time with Hank Shocklee and Flavor Flav at Long Island’s WBAU as part of the story of how Public Enemy began.

item.title: Ye Closes U.S. Stadium Run With Big Sean And A Return To “Street Lights”
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Ye brought Big Sean out for three songs in Glendale and reached back to 808s & Heartbreak for his U.S. stadium finale.
item.content:encoded:
Ye brought Big Sean back onstage as he closed out his announced 2026 U.S. stadium dates Saturday night (November 21).

At State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Arizona, the two went back to their G.O.O.D. Music catalog before Ye reached deeper into his own for “Street Lights.”

The Glendale setlist includes “Mercy,” “Clique,” and Sean’s “I Don’t Fuck With You.” Sean performed E-40’s verse a cappella during his own song.

The guest spot followed their September reunion at Chicago’s Soldier Field. They performed those three songs there, too. In Chicago, 2 Chainz joined them for “Mercy” on both nights.

The Glendale show followed stops in Dallas and Houston, where Ye brought out Playboi Carti on Halloween. The next stadium date listed on Ye’s tour site is March 19, 2027, at Estadio Banorte in Mexico City.

Sean has traced their relationship back to a Detroit radio station, where he asked Ye to hear him rap while he was still in high school.

He told WHO?MAG he caught Ye on his way out of the station, where he had been promoting Late Registration.

“He told me I only have 16 bars, but I rapped for 10 minutes,” Sean recalled. Ye went on to sign him to G.O.O.D. Music.

By 2012, Sean and Ye were trading verses on “Mercy” with Pusha T and 2 Chainz and sharing “Clique” with Jay-Z.

They later aired their differences in separate Drink Champs appearances. Sean used his own interview to respond after Ye criticized signing him.

Sean said he took the criticism personally but still credited Ye with giving him his break.

“He changed my life and I love him for that,” Sean said.

item.title: Killer Mike’s Greenwood Shuts Down Its Banking Program
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Killer Mike's Greenwood ends its banking program, with remaining balances set to go back to customers by paper check.
item.content:encoded:
Killer Mike helped launch Greenwood to give Black and Latino customers another place to bank.

That option closed November 19, when Greenwood ended its banking program with Coastal Community Bank and shut all accounts under the program.

The cutoff ended debit card access, direct deposits, transfers and bill payments, according to Greenwood’s customer notice. The company said payments sent to a Greenwood account after the cutoff would go back to the sender.

The money left in those accounts isn’t going to another app. Greenwood says Coastal Community Bank will mail checks for the remaining balances by December 2, and customers have until November 24 to confirm their mailing address through Greenwood support.

Greenwood announced the shutdown timeline in October alongside a partnership with DreamFi, the financial technology company co-founded by civil rights attorney Ben Crump.

Customers can choose whether to apply to DreamFi, and Greenwood says it isn’t transferring accounts or customer information automatically.

“Economic empowerment has always been inseparable from civil rights. This partnership between Greenwood and DreamFi ensures that the important work will grow,” Greenwood co-founder Andrew Young said in the announcement.

“From day one, Greenwood has been about more than banking. It’s been about economic justice and creating opportunities for wealth creation in communities that have been historically excluded,” Crump said.

Killer Mike, Young and Bounce TV founder Ryan Glover introduced Greenwood in 2020, starting with spending and savings accounts designed for Black and Latino communities. Killer Mike had been urging people to support Black-owned banks before the launch.

The founders raised $3 million in seed funding before the launch and pitched Greenwood as a way to give customers more control over where their money went.

Greenwood raised another $85 million over two rounds, bringing its publicly announced funding to $88 million. Truist Ventures led a $40 million round in 2021, and Pendulum Holdings led a $45 million round in 2022.

Their original pitch included donations tied to debit card purchases and monthly grants for Black or Latino small-business owners.

Greenwood wasn’t a bank itself.

Coastal provided the banking services behind the app, while DreamFi is a separate company that uses FinWise Bank and doesn’t currently offer a standalone savings account. Under the offer Greenwood announced for its customers, DreamFi membership costs $9.99 a month after the first 30 days.

The closure also puts a deadline on retrieving paperwork. Greenwood says customers can still pull statements from the app through December 22, and the last one will cover transactions that posted through closing.

Greenwood says customers who earned interest in 2026 will get a tax form by January 31, 2027.

item.title: Nick Cannon’s Wild ‘N Out Live Postpones Several Arena Shows After Hospitalization
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Nick Cannon's Wild 'N Out Live postponed stops in Houston, Atlanta and other cities. Here's what ticket holders need to know.
item.content:encoded:
Nick Cannon‘s Wild ‘N Out Live tour has postponed at least seven arena shows, including last night’s stop at Houston’s Toyota Center.

The postponements come as Cannon asked fans for prayers from a hospital bed. In an Instagram reel, he wore a face mask and used “#LupusWarrior” in the caption. Cannon did not say why he was in the hospital, and the venues did not link the postponements to his health.

The Houston venue hasn’t announced a replacement date, but fans who already bought tickets can still use them when the show is rescheduled.

“At this time, we don’t have information on a new date,” the Toyota Center said.

Fans who purchased directly through AXS can sign in to their accounts and request a refund as long as they didn’t transfer, list or sell the tickets.

Anyone who received tickets from somebody else must send them back to the original buyer before that person can request a refund.

Houston’s venue said it won’t process refunds for resale tickets or tickets bought through a third-party site. It said eligible refunds would go back to the card used for the purchase and could take up to 30 business days to process.

Atlanta’s State Farm Arena also postponed its December 1 show and said existing tickets and parking would carry over.

Charlotte’s December 2 show is on hold as well. Live Nation lists Miami, Tampa, Indianapolis and the original Chicago finale as postponed. The notices do not give a reason.

Live Nation initially billed The Next Generation as a 20-city tour from Oakland to Chicago.

Its arena shows bring the freestyle battles and improv games from Cannon’s TV series to the stage, with live performances and guest appearances that can change from city to city.

Cannon was talking about taking the show on the road in 2005, the year Wild ‘N Out debuted on MTV. “We are going to take the show on the road with all the cats from the show,” he told AllHipHop after MTV picked up the series for a second season.

By 2017, the tour had booked two arena shows on the same night, with one in Maryland and the other in Washington, D.C. The lineup for that doubleheader included Wale and Yo Gotti alongside the show’s comics.

item.title: Wendy Williams’ Lawyer Says Guardian Refused Thanksgiving Trip
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Joe Tacopina says Wendy Williams' guardian refused a Miami visit and a Nov. 6 conference was canceled without a new date.
item.content:encoded:
Wendy Williams wants to spend Thanksgiving with her family in Miami, but her personal lawyer says her court-appointed guardian has refused to let her go.

Joe Tacopina said he was still pressing for an answer as the holiday approached.

In an interview on 77 WABC’s Sid & Friends in the Morning, Tacopina said Williams was willing to make the trip with the security she is required to use.

“The guardian said, no, she can’t go,” he said. He said he hadn’t been given a reason.

Tacopina said this wasn’t the first time Williams needed permission for an outing. He recalled that she had to get approval before joining him and Rosenberg for lunch.

The travel dispute comes as Williams is still trying to end the guardianship that began in 2022. Tacopina said a court conference scheduled for November 6 had been canceled and that there was “no new date put on the calendar.”

Tacopina made clear that Williams hired him as her personal lawyer, not as her attorney in the guardianship proceeding itself.

“So we have to get her in front of a judge,” he said.

He joined Williams’ legal team in 2025 after representing A$AP Rocky in the trial that ended with the rapper’s acquittal.

Williams has spoken publicly about wanting the arrangement to end.

“It’s time for my money and my life to get back to status quo,” she said in an earlier appearance on ABC’s The View, making it clear that replacing her guardian was not her end goal.

The state guardianship itself is sealed, as a public order in a separate federal case notes.

In a statement about the guardianship reported by ABC News in 2025, a lawyer for guardian Sabrina Morrissey denied wrongdoing and said the court supervises her work.

Williams built her national following in radio, including a syndicated afternoon show she began in 2001 at New York’s WBLS, and was inducted into the Radio Hall of Fame in 2009.

She later moved into daytime TV, hosting a syndicated talk show that ran for 13 seasons.

Peacock plans to revisit those years in 2027 in a three-part documentary with the working title Clap If You Care: The Wendy Williams Show.

item.title: Swae Lee Halts Set & Calls For Security After Being Pelted With Beer
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Swae Lee stops the music in Shillong and asks security to remove a concertgoer before getting back to his festival set.
item.content:encoded:
Swae Lee stopped his set at India’s Shillong Cherry Blossom Festival after a drink was reportedly thrown toward him on November 21.

The Rae Sremmurd rapper pointed into the crowd and asked security to remove a concertgoer before getting back to the performance.

The interruption came on the festival’s final night at the Madan Kurkalang Sports Complex in Bhoirymbong, outside Shillong.

Swae Lee pointed toward people at the front and accused someone there of throwing beer.

“You gotta go,” Swae Lee told the person, according to Northeast Live’s account of a clip from the show. The station reported that he wiped his face and asked security to identify the person.

He asked for a towel before resuming his set.

At a Rae Sremmurd show in Dallas in August 2018, a phone thrown from the crowd hit Swae Lee in the mouth while the duo performed “Powerglide.” He finished the set and said afterward that he’d needed stitches.

His performance in India was part of a two-day festival that paired international acts with musicians from Meghalaya and the surrounding region. The state’s tourism office listed Swae Lee among the headliners and billed the event around the seasonal flowering that gives the festival its name.

The festival booked Nelly for its opening night. Khalid and Swedish electronic duo Galantis performed on the closing night alongside Swae Lee.

The Shillong date followed Swae Lee’s November 2025 appearance at Rolling Loud India in Navi Mumbai.

Swae Lee was already familiar to festival audiences as one half of Rae Sremmurd, the duo behind “Black Beatles.” He also shares one of his biggest solo credits with Post Malone on “Sunflower,” the song the pair recorded for Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse.

Northeast Live reported a separate interruption during Khalid’s set that night when a shirt was thrown toward the singer, who continued performing.

Swae Lee is due back on the road in March, when he joins Jhené Aiko’s 37-city North American tour, which opens in St. Louis.
